chapters.title: The colour of a test
chapters.speech: A bright yellow solution turns orange when cyanide is introduced. But does the colour change actually identify one ion, or only something about the mixture?
chapters.source: 2019 Analytical Methods 11:5169–5176; original author-archived four-panel photograph and absorption data.

chapters.title: The original scientific record
chapters.speech: This is the published experiment, not a substitute stock photograph. The four panels record absorption, visible colour, fluorescence emission, and the vials under ultraviolet light.
chapters.source: Owner archive figure-cyanide-sensor.jpg, visual panels a–d; RSC DOI 10.1039/C9AY01557D. Figure numbering pending original PDF inspection.

chapters.title: What changes in solution
chapters.speech: The test was in ninety percent acetonitrile and ten percent water. Curcumin began yellow, while added cyanide produced a striking orange solution. This is not a water-only assay.
chapters.source: 2019 study Abstract: CH3CN:H2O 90:10; curcumin visible yellow-to-orange response; archived panel b.

chapters.title: Two spectral landmarks
chapters.speech: The original absorbance figure gives the numerical story. The original band at four hundred twenty-one nanometres decreases, while a strong signal emerges at five hundred twenty. The shift is ninety-nine nanometres.
chapters.source: 2019 article measured UV-vis values 421 and 520 nm, shift 99 nm; original panel a.

chapters.title: Selectivity is conditional
chapters.speech: Most tested monovalent anions caused no comparable response. Hydroxide is the important exception: it also changed the colour. That caveat belongs beside the claim of cyanide sensing.
chapters.source: 2019 article lists controls F−, Cl−, Br−, I−, acetate, dihydrogen arsenate, azide; hydroxide similar more intense response.

chapters.title: The light dims
chapters.speech: Curcumin emits fluorescence around five hundred twenty nanometres. Adding cyanide quenched that emission. These are the actual fluorescence results, accompanied by photographed sample vials.
chapters.source: 2019 paper fluorescence at 520 nm and quenching; original four-panel figure panels c/d.

chapters.title: A cellular observation
chapters.speech: Curcumin fluorescence was also observed in living cells. After cyanide was added, the signal slowly faded over time. The schematic here is illustrative; it is not a fabricated cell image.
chapters.source: 2019 article reports living-cell fluorescence and slow quenching; source microscopy image not staged, therefore never fabricated.

chapters.title: What the result does not mean
chapters.speech: The reported detection limit was two point three micromolar. The solvent mixture, hydroxide interference, and slow cellular response limit how broadly we can interpret this finding.
chapters.source: 2019 article lower limit 2.3 × 10^-6 molar, 90:10 CH3CN-water, hydroxide response and cell time dependence.
